mission.title: Smoke
mission.description: Find out who stole the topographic data on the no-fly zone from under the Merovingian's nose.

npc.say: Stealing from the Merovingian--it's unthinkable! Whoever did it will die in unspeakable agony. But...hrm...if any are judged guilty of negligence, they'll almost certainly be punished, too.
It couldn't have been an outsider... There's no scent--except yours.
Hrr, of course we three aren't the only ones who watch this area. The others come and go...but there's always someone here.

End transmission.
Reactivate the jammers. I want perimeter reports from--

phase.briefing:
The General's Sentinels think they detected a ship of the type supposedly used by the intruders, just before they were hit by a missile barrage. That's all well and good, but if the General--who survived, unfortunately--thinks it excuses him from finishing the job of extracting data from that network he found out there, he's in for a surprise.
He's scheduled to beam in a broadcast now. Go make sure he knows the score, operative.

enter.say: The General's radio boy should be waiting for you in there. Coast looks clear.

objective.text: Talk to the General's radio operator

done.say: Another missile strike? Wow, doesn't sound like things are going too well out there.

phase.briefing:
You know, operative, there are many recorded cases of soldiers in human wars intentionally giving themselves minor injuries in order to avoid going into battle. I wouldn't be at all surprised if that's what the General is doing: inventing ridiculous stories of intruder ships and missile strikes, while he and his men are actually having the time of their lives out there in the no-fly zone, out of range of all sensors.
I've just been notified of an equally disgusting problem, but at least this one I can do something about: someone has stolen the topographic data on the no-fly zone. The General should still have a copy, of course, but oh, we've oh-so-conveniently just lost contact with him again. I smell a rat, operative, and you're going to go smoke it out. Get over to the scene of the crime.

enter.say: The data was listed off a computer, right out from under some of our Exiles. Whoever snagged it must have been pretty good to get past their noses undetected.

talk.say: Stealing from the Merovingian--it's unthinkable! Whoever did it will die in unspeakable agony. But...hrm...if any are judged guilty of negligence, they'll almost certainly be punished, too.
It couldn't have been an outsider... There's no scent--except yours.
Hrr, of course we three aren't the only ones who watch this area. The others come and go...but there's always someone here.

complete.say: Hm... So someone got the data out of there without leaving a trace--not even a hint of a scent that would give them away.

phase.briefing:
Glub, glub, glub! Do you know what that sound is, operative? It's the sound of me drowning in the incompetence of subordinates!
We just had rowdies at a location nearby call in some sort of alert about a suspicious character, but now we can't raise them. Just wait, I'm sure you'll get there to find them in a drunken stupor in the middle of a party, and they'll call it a missile strike...

enter.say: Doesn't look like much of a party in there to me. I'm not picking up any activity, as a matter of fact.

done.say: That idiot, the General, finally sorted out his personal problems sufficiently to get back in contact. He should be coming through now.

talk.say: I've been informed of the data theft. I'm having a copy of my version of the topographic data sent back to you.

done.say:
End transmission.
Reactivate the jammers. I want perimeter reports from--

phase.briefing:
So he's just fine, imagine that... I can see right through his smoke and mirrors, {player}. Years of dealing with slacking operatives have taught me a trick or two.
We're running a scan around your area for a match of the General's copy of the stolen file. Shouldn't be long before we have our culprit red-handed.
Ah, that would be them now. Try to take them alive.

enter.say: I'm getting something, but...it's hard to pin down. Working on it...

done.say:
The data's already been uploaded.
Thank the Frenchman for me. It would have been much more difficult to get it from the Machines.
What th--? That weird broadcast signal cut out, and he dropped like his strings were cut. He didn't sound much like a lupine, either. Something funny's going on here.

near.say:
A dire lupine? So that's why the others didn't spot an intruder!
I'm picking up weird activity on him. There's an external signal--some kind of broadcast...but it isn't using standard encryption.

mission.finish: It wasn't a lupine, {player}--not anymore, at any rate. I'm fairly sure that was Mauser, the fellow Zion's been chasing around the city. He's been hacking phone lines right and left, it seems, which has put the Machines in a foul mood, but now he's really crossed the line by stealing from us.
